documents_money: Passport/ID, driver's license (+ International Driving Permit if you're a non-EU visitor — see Practical Info → Connectivity & Money)
Rental car booking confirmation + credit card the booking was made on (many rental counters require it)
Travel insurance details (policy number + assistance line, saved on phone and printed/screenshotted)
A physical backup of your accommodation address in Italian, for taxi drivers/emergencies: Via San Michele Arcangelo 24, 96017 Noto (SR)
Some euro cash (see Practical Info → Connectivity & Money for notes on unreliable ATMs and cash-preferred spots)
EU plug adapters if coming from outside continental Europe
beach_water_gear: Swimsuits (bring 2 each — hard to fully dry overnight with daily beach use)
Water shoes — Eloro and Calamosche both have rocky entry points, also useful for snorkeling
Snorkel mask if you have your own preferred fit (boat tours provide gear, but personal masks fit better)
Quick-dry beach towels — separate from villa towels, since you'll want these damp in the car, not the bathroom
A collapsible/pop-up beach shade or umbrella — Calamosche, Marianelli, Eloro, and Vendicari have zero shade infrastructure
Dry bag — for phones/wallets on the boat trip or wild beaches
Reef-safe sunscreen (considerate for the marine reserves you'll be swimming in), and after-sun/aloe
Underwater phone case or an old phone, if you want boat/snorkel photos without risking your main one
hiking_gear: Real hiking shoes or trail runners — Cava Grande's descent is steep and loose underfoot, sandals aren't enough
A daypack per couple/person for water + snacks on hikes
Refillable water bottles — bring more than feels necessary, both hike write-ups specifically warn about the climb back up in heat
Mosquito repellent — Vendicari reserve is a wetland, reviews mention mosquitoes at dusk
A hat/cap and sunglasses with a strap (useful for both hiking and the boat)
clothing: A light layer or cardigan for evenings — nights cool to ~18-20°C even on hot days (2026-07-21 addendum: climatological data for the exact trip window suggests evenings may run cooler than that, possibly low-to-mid teens °C by early October — pack slightly warmer than this estimate to be safe; see Practical Info → Rainy / Windy Day Backup Options for the fuller note)

One "nice" outfit each for the Michelin-starred dinners (Crocifisso, Cortile Spirito Santo, Duomo) — smart-casual is fine, none of these are strict black-tie, but Duomo in particular skews a bit dressier (Accursio in Modica lost its Michelin star for the 2026 guide and is no longer a tasting-menu venue — see the Radici entry in Explore — so it no longer needs this outfit)
Something you don't mind getting dusty/scraped for the hikes
A wind-resistant layer for the boat trip — it's noticeably breezier on the water, even on a warm day
health_toiletries: Personal medications (enough for the full week + a couple of spare days)
Basic first-aid — plasters, antiseptic, motion sickness tablets (for the boat), rehydration salts
Sunscreen (face + body, high SPF — the group skews "very adventurous," which hopefully extends to reapplying)
electronics: A portable power bank — useful for full beach/boat days away from outlets
Offline maps downloaded (Google Maps offline area for southeastern Sicily) in case of patchy rural signal
SIM/eSIM sorted before or on arrival (see Practical Info → Connectivity & Money)
